newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 26.

text.p: of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.

- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, said the Irish government's file of evidence on the Bloody Sunday killings in Northern Ireland probably warranted a further full inquiry. - Ireland's rural water charges lobby is reserving its position on fielding general election candidates after the Irish government's announcement of a 7.23 million punt package of subsidies to 145,000 householders. - About 800,000 punts worth of football tops were stolen from a Walkinstown warehouse in Dublin on Tuesday. - Independent Irish airline Ryanair is gearing up for a stock-market floatation which could value the airline at about 250 million punts.

- The Irish government on Tuesday began a big buy-out of special interest groups to clear the way for a May general election. - Ireland's film industry is set for a major boost when the Finance Bill is published on Wednesday.
- European share and bond markets rallied strongly on Tuesday
ahead of the quarter point rise in U.S. interest rates with Dublin shares jumping over 350 million punts in value.
- The Irish government on Tuesday expressed confidence that Environment Minister Brendan Howlin's bid to end the row over rural water charges will remove the issue from the general election agenda.

- The Irish government, increasingly under pressure from low-paid shop-workers working for the large multiple chains, on Wednesday accepted a measure from the main opposition party Fianna Fail which will allow the workers refuse to work on Sundays.
